question: What was the estimated capital expenditure of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways in India for the financial year 2024-25?
solution:
The correct answer is __**₹2.72 lakh crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) in India had an estimated capital expenditure of **₹2.72 lakh crore** for the financial year 2024-25.
 
• This allocation aimed to accelerate the construction of national highways and improve road infrastructure across the country.
 
• The increased budget allocation was part of the Indian government's focus on enhancing connectivity and supporting economic growth.
 
• The capital expenditure for MoRTH has been steadily increasing in recent years, reflecting the government's commitment to infrastructure development.
 
• This funding supports projects such as the Bharatmala Pariyojana, aimed at developing economic corridors and expressways.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatmala Pariyojana:**

 
 
• A flagship program launched by the Indian government to develop highways and economic corridors across the country.
 
• It aims to improve freight movement, reduce travel time, and enhance overall connectivity.
 
• The program includes the construction of expressways, bridges, and bypasses to boost infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **National Infrastructure Pipeline (NIP):**
 
 
• The NIP is a government initiative aimed at providing world-class infrastructure across India.
 
• It includes projects in sectors like transportation, energy, water, and communication.
 
• Road infrastructure plays a significant role in the NIP, with substantial funding allocated to MoRTH projects.
 
 
 
• **Gati Shakti Master Plan:**
 
 
• Launched by the Indian government to integrate and coordinate infrastructure projects for seamless connectivity.
 
• This initiative focuses on the synergy between road, rail, air, and waterways for effective logistics management.
 
 
 
• **Public-Private Partnerships (PPP) in Road Infrastructure:**
 
 
• India extensively uses PPP models for road construction and maintenance to ensure efficient project execution.
 
• PPP models like Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) and Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM) are widely adopted.
